对比之前的Demo很难说有啥变化，甚至连语言切到简体中文时会出现各种各样的bug的情况也保留了下来，我是没记住当初Demo里面是不是用中文进不去太空站然后切了英文。反正一局都没打完就老老实实又切回英文了。 另外，这个游戏作为一个爬塔打牌，局外成长内容给得极为吝啬与有限，除了几个成就一样的“改造”，玩家每次失败的游戏并不能为以后的游戏积累任何优势。然后好死不死的这游戏虽然是爬塔，但是地图跟隔壁集〇战略一样只能看见下一步，很多时候，既看不见目标点所属的势力，也看不见目标点到底是事件还是战斗还是精英战斗。只有零零散散的几个点是揭示出来的，于是就基本无从进行路线规划。 总之，目前阶段并不推荐购买，即便语言方面不够成障碍，这游戏本身的乐趣现阶段也相当有限。

Very very barebone at the moment. I understand Alpha... but this is not the kind of game to release in alpha in my opinion. Balance is insanely out of whack. Rogue like yes, but barely any control whatsoever on anything it feels completely based on RNG. Very constraint exploration, very low choice of modules, ROI on encounters is very random. I can't put my finger exactly on the issue. Great core mechanics, great potential. No one was waiting for this title so why release it and potentially get flooded with bad reviews ? It's already mixed and people will, I assume, avoid it. Great mystery. Give it a year or two and it will probably be nice. At this moment, not recommended.

[h1]别有洞天的星舰卡牌对战[/h1] 在肉鸽卡牌游戏越来越卷的年代，如何在这片红海中做出差异化无疑是相当具有挑战的。以组建船体模块、卡费自由转换以及舰体部位伤害为三大核心机制的本作无疑是相当具有特点和创新精神的。游戏的背景设定是在浩瀚缥缈的星空之中，类型游戏传统的“爬塔”也在本作中化为了极其多样的星舰前进路线。由于舰体各方面都可以定制，使得本作的策略深度很高，也有着不错的自由度。星舰对战的轰鸣声与爆炸后的绚烂烟花也有不错的感官体验。 [h1]精准出击 整体和部分的有机统一[/h1] 正如前文所言，相较于市面上较为同质化的一众肉鸽卡牌，本作在机制上还是相当独特的。因此去过一遍做成新手教程的序章还是相当有必要的。简单来说本作的卡组其实就是对应飞船的不同模块，也可以称为组件。例如安装上脉冲激光就可以获得一套激光类型的卡牌，装配上屏障护盾则是生成一套字面意义上的防御卡牌，还有什么导弹、高射炮序列卡牌等等。在战斗结算卡牌奖励的时候，同样也是根据模块选择卡牌，总的来说均衡自己的攻守之势是相当有必要的。 具体到战斗环节也十分特别。首先传统意义上的卡费被分解成了能器、能量和能质红绿蓝三色。玩家可以自由调节每回合三色卡费的恢复点数，但是也不能说咱就孤注一掷全部倾向于偏攻击的红色了，因为那会导致飞船过热并最终造成船体受损。每一种卡牌都会消耗不同的三色点数，因此卡费冗余是非常正常的，但是优点是可以留到下一回合。 其次我们在具体对战时，可以选择攻击整个船体也能够精准打击某个部分（会对应敌方相应的卡牌组件）。光打击部分可能一时无法使得整个船体倾覆，但是会使得该部位哑火，在得到维修前对应的卡牌就会失效。实战中非常常见的做法就是优先打击对方的强火力部位导致其丧失战斗能力，然后再慢慢消磨整个舰体。而常见的所谓“意图”会以行动格的方式呈现，敌方卡牌下的格子填满就会发动卡牌效果。除了常规防御外，像是制导导弹之类的也能通过特定的卡牌进行阻截。 此外游戏在音画表现上也很好地运用了飞船对战的题材优势。战斗时敌我双方的战舰分别占据一半屏幕，看起来就十分具有张力。各种攻击造成的爆炸特效十分炫酷，甚至防御卡牌也会以能量罩的特效可视化呈现，细节拉满了。 [h1]总结[/h1] 相当具有创新精神的太空星舰题材卡牌肉鸽。不过内容体量上还有待拓充，而且有部分汉化不完整的问题，期待正式版的发布。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

Don't buy this game if you're over the age of 30, as this game is not appropriate for those that lack great eyesight. Though the game seems like it might be fun to play, it's not really playable by anyone that doesn't have great eyesight. The game has a bit of dialogue, but they force it into small boxes with a small & narrow font that makes reading quite a challenge. It's really quite surprising they made that decision, as there's plenty of blank space in the UI to use a larger font. Still valid as of July 29, 2025.

This review comes after 10 gameplays. This game difficulty is very difficult. It's not a challenge, it's pure flat impossible to reach half-way and once out of ten tries to reach the end node before the final boss, and being destroyed. Whatever happened between the last reviewer and Jan.2025, this gameplay sucks. All ship classes have no god-given way of surviving half-way through the second game system after the first five node systems. The RNG card selections are 75% in the enemy's favor. All of my ship classes, even with upgrades along the way, breach shields and hull before reaching the nearest space station for any hope of repairs. The onboard engineers in repair a piddly 4 hull points of 50, and whoa, here comes another enemy ship, full hard 50 hullpoints. Oh? Survived that? Get only 27 credits, not even enough to buy a bowl of RAMEN. Can't upgrade squat. FIX IT: Add a space station every three nodes, increase the credit payout, reset or decrease the crew cooldowns at the start of each battle. Space is hard, this game has awesome graphics, but survivability is horrible. I'll take my money back and buy a more satisfying game like Eve Online.

I kinda hate this game, because I'm garbage at it. I want to like it. I love games where you can customize your ships, make tactical choices, etc., it just feels like the game mechanics of this game make that neigh impossible. I completed the tutorial then moved into the first real map and tried getting through it about eight times. Every time I'd get about halfway through before being destroyed. The thing that irks me? You make no progress when you die. It's not like a roguelike game where you die but at least get a slight improvement from it. No, you get nothing unless you complete the map. So dying just feels like a huge waste of my time. Half of the time I died because I ran out of fuel. After a couple runs I figured out how fuel works and all that, but the game seems to put you in this almost impossible situation where you have to choose: do I grind for money to buy upgrades so I can actually complete the map, or do I pay for fuel and ship repairs? If I don't pay for fuel and ship repairs at a station, I get forced to fight the boss and I die. If I pay for fuel and ship repairs, I barely have anything left to make any upgrades and generally still end up getting killed. The game just ended up frustrating my severely. I wanted to like it, but couldn't get far enough to actually enjoy any of it.

Idk what's with the negative reviews for this game. Y'all never played FTL and it shows. Breachway is super unforgiving, but not unfair. Every lost run can easily be traced to some unfortunate mistake. The game doesn't blindside you with some "oop, sucks to be u" elite encounter that shreds you to pieces. If that happens, that's probably cause you were too greedy. Sure, I've never won a run yet, but I came close. And every time my ship was blown up I didn't go "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ devs, worst game ever", but "uh oh, shouldn't have taken that risk". So, I'd suggest ignoring the Mostly Positive rating. If Breachway sounds interesting, try it and see if you like what it offers. If you don't, here's always the refund option.

Even after the updates. Still unbelievably one sided and not enjoyable in the slightest. The fact that enemy missile ships just have unlimited missiles illustrates this point the best. Or here's your random elite encounter that you got screwed into with no way to avoid it. Oh we're going to fire missile destroying flak every turn, shield every turn, and have 160 HP to your 50. What a joke. Also, solid bug that just stopped my missiles from reaching their target. Just floating out in space doing absolutely nothing. --------------------------------------- This game is honestly terrible. It feels like a random number generator with a game on top of it but with the added eff you of making all the encounters perfectly counter your ship loadout. Did you take the flak cannon from the mysterious stranger? Every ship you fight will have shields. Did you take the ion cannon instead? Who cares, the ships won't have shields anymore. The fact that the second or third ships you fight have a turn one ability that just gives them an extra flak round is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've never seen that weapon as a card option, ever. At least FTL had some redeeming qualities that after struggling you would get better. Not here though. After 6 hours, my best run was the FIRST one I did. Everything after that has been a disaster. I wish I could get a refund.

Graphics and game concept are good. After the update the game feels like you could play any ship and have a chance; however.... It is 100% against you. You could have a phenomenal build , but lo and behold an enemy ship (especially in the second system) is the near perfect counter to your build, and then after surviving that conflict (to which you'll most likely suffer severe damage) RNGeezus just so happens to make every node to the next space station a conflict zone...notwithstanding your relations to whatever faction in that zone. So be prepared to be screwed over at every opportunity, no matter how well you think you understand this game, RNGeezus says screw you. I forgot to add this as well, the heat mechanic is absolutely broken...towards you, and it make no fracking sense. So you see cards that will give you heat if played, or dealt to you with enemies, which makes sense...but then get heat on playing things that don't tell you they generate heat. Now you try to be the heat dispenser guy...too bad the AI have better capacity and/or dissipation than you ever will. I'm revising this on the fact that I can't play this anymore, the heat mechanic is absolutely broken against you...as of this review I would've beat the second boss, but heat killed me on literally the last turn to kill said boss. I played few heat generation cards, have radiators equipped and upgraded, took relatively little heat from the boss, shielded often and attacked every turn, but the heat just kept building, never venting...it was practically the perfect build (Avalanche in case you're wondering)...but it still isn't enough. Player ships need to have better heat management because as it stands you're not going to win against the 'final' boss. 05JUN2025: I decided to play a little after this recent update to see if anything of useful note takes place...it doesn't. Heat is even worse against you...the enemies have a card that makes you loss coolant for each shield card you play...not to mention the heat build up in general has gotten even more insane. The ships definitely had better heat management before v1.9.

The game's primary conceit is cool for all of 2 hours. And then you realize you're just playing Slay the Spire, except for some reason the game only lets you put 4 block cards into your deck , which kind of guarantees you won't draw them when you need them on the early turns. Oh sure, you can reset fights until the rng doesn't ♥♥♥♥ you over, but who the ♥♥♥♥ has time for that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? All lot of the concepts are interesting and cool. And terribly executed with little thought to how fluid it makes the game. There's far too many problems that aren't just simple fixes for me to actually recommend this game.

[h1]Breachway: FTL’s Hot Cousin With Card Addiction[/h1] Bought the game thinking I’d command a badass spaceship crew across the galaxy. Ended up arguing with my weapons system and rage-quitting because the second boss gave me trust issues. [i]Great game. Would cry in the cockpit again.[/i] [b]Pros:[/b] Card-based space combat that’s more tactical than my dating life. Weapon loadouts that actually matter. Laser? Missile? Hack into their mainframe and delete their hopes? You choose. Each ship feels distinct. I tried the “fire ship” and just committed arson for 3 sectors. Looks and sounds good enough to trick me into thinking I'm doing something meaningful with my life. [b]Cons:[/b] – Currently has more potential than content. Two bosses, and then... existential silence. – Some cards feel like filler material from a failed Star Trek episode. – UI sometimes behaves like it’s also in early access. I misclicked once and got ghosted by an entire neutral station. – The Firebrand is great… if you like [i]losing slowly[/i]. Shields say no. [h2]Suggestions (aka things that made me question reality):[/h2] • Give us more maps, more bosses, and maybe a reason why I’m flying toward this signal besides "just vibes." • Some heat-based weapons feel like lukewarm disappointment. • Let me get new weapons more often. I’m tired of begging black market traders like it’s Steam Summer Sale. • Please fix how power management feels like unpaid mental labor. [b]Final thoughts:[/b] This game is what happens when Slay the Spire goes to space and accidentally downloads FTL’s trauma. I love it. I hate it. I want more. [b]Final Rating: 7.8/10 – Needs more bosses, fewer bugs, and maybe a therapist system for my ship crew.[/b] [hr] PS: I finished the two bosses in under 6 hours. The rest of my time? Staring at my deck, wondering if I should’ve become a space-farmer instead. Still recommended. Just… don’t expect closure.

This game is beyond trash/10 1. It does NOTHING right for the roguelike gameplay and i mean absolutely NOTHING. You cannot make builds, you never get money, you never get items, you never get good cards, you never get drops, you can't basically heal (the option on the station is worthless and cost more money than the total amount you make during all encounters to get there put together), it's literally impossible to progress unless an insane amount of luck is involved and you play 1 specific ship with 1 specific build (that is literally the ONLY one you can actually get pass the first map in a statistically sane manner). 2. The map and events are non existent. It's perma combat even if you are max reputation with a faction and you go in that faction's territory. There are a million games that did this a million times better for example Knock on the Coffin Lid which is a completely retarded game also but at least they had half a braincell to get the map design right and not have you in perma combat. 3. There is 0 skill factor to this game. You can't make builds. If you have a total of 10 cards in the deck and 2 are shields you somehow won't get the shields not even in 20 draws. It's pathetic how bad it is. Couldn't even get the card draw straight, couldn't even get the total cards in hand straight, couldn't even get a decent balance on the energy regulator which was a good idea but executed with the feet. It's almost as if the devs never played their game and intentionally missed every possible target of what a roguelike experience should be. If you want a proper deck builder play Monster Train 2. That game respects your time, respects the build and most importantly it lets you actually play the build. It does not overpunish, it allows you to heal, it offers a challenge without being retarded, it has a shop where you can actually buy everything you need as opposed to letting you stare at all the things you literally cannot buy AT ALL not even if you save all money and put together. This game didn't even try to be fake like Hades where it gives you the illusion that you can win right off the bat, and afterwards it gets retarded.... nope ..... this game went full retarded right from the start and i personally wonder how you can ♥♥♥♥ up 2+2=4 in 2025 this bad. How did you manage not to get 1 single good aspect in your game after all this development time..... HOW?! I was even patient with this since i didn't want to blast it right away in hopes that they would fix the issues since it was so painfully obvious the game is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ broken but it did not happen. I can't recommend this game not even if it's free it's an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Don't know if I can recommend this game in its current iteration. The fuel system sucks and I mean SUCKS. It's the single thing that can literally make the game unplayable. Want to explore? Too bad. Want to check out that mysterious node? Too bad. Git gud. Or conversely magically manifest fuel out of nothing in between the start and the stations 20 nodes away. Just give me the option to explore and fight and add fuel a little easier.

Solid start for early access. Definitely needs more sectors (only 2 as of the writing of this review) and more bosses / enemies for added variety. I've got 7 hours into the game, will definitely play through multiple runs with all the different ships and weapon loadouts. Feels like a nice mix of StS and FTL. I would say that the map choices need to have a bit more agency to them. As it stands you're just trying to run through as many fights as possible with little else for objectives. Sure, there are a few "quest" options sprinkled in, but so far they don't feel particularly meaningful / important. Most important thing is hunting as many elite fights as you can and getting equipment and card choices + credits.

I wanted to like this game, but it needs a lot of balancing. Every node is "prepare for battle". Even "friendly" nodes. So, what's the point in having different relations? The enemies have more systems to try and manage than is possible, so each round is basically trying to keep your damage from destroying you. Each run should make you feel stronger, but it doesn't. I've beaten Elden ring, and Lords of the Fallen, so it's not that it's 'hard'. It's just not balanced to reward skill.

This game started out good, but it is _designed_ for you to lose over and over and over again. Everything will try your patience and annoy you. Will you find the equipment you need? Probably not. It's a very sad thumbs down, because I really *want* to like this game, but 150 hours and a year later, it just doesn't feel like it's coming together. The power allotment and heat management systems are a fun. Crew abilities, equipment/loadout changes, are great, but at the end of the day, most runs are simply not fun. The brittle, hacking, overheat mechanics are all neat ideas, but they all lose out to raw damage 90% of the time. Then, in the raw damage department, it often comes down to which colors you want to use to do 6 damage with. While there are some great synergies, and weapon procs, it can be cumbersome to calculate. [ok, if this adds +1 shred, this attack will do too much shred and trigger its brittle proc instead of this other card. But they have 4 shield, a 5 damage weapon with 2 shred + 1 shred from the last card will do how much?] It is far simpler to go with a laser/railgun build and just target the systems you want to cripple. The same applies to hacking/ion. You can have an absolutely OP build with either, but only if you pick up a lucky item. You can't really take an ion cannon with crappy cards in the start and turn it into a great ion build. And on that note, it's still very hard to lean into whatever build you are working towards. The only mechanic that truly works is upgraded cards of any type. You can have 3 flak cannons installed and have less output as a laser/flak/missile combo with a couple upgraded cards. You are forced to pick vanilla cards in the beginning, just to have enough cards to win battles. So, by the time you have enough money to upgrade that beam weapon you love, all the spots are filled with junk. If you can afford the draft upgrade, then you still have to pay to remove everything, and then *hope* you get some better draws, all while fighting the next couple battles without enough cards. If you get lucky and find the perfect module to go with that beam weapon, it's not going to happen. Even if you wanted to go all in and sell your missile launcher and PDC, you can't afford the module and draft upgrade, even if you were willing to suck up a bunch of damage over the next few combats, have insufficient reactor power, and then *still* need some luck to get a good card. I know resource management, luck, and tough choices are part of any good rogue-like, but most runs feel like a slog. You're somewhat railroaded into taking whatever weapon type you get a lucky card start/draw on. Even with sacrifices, you can't really buy or guide your way into wherever you were heading. ie: If I have two flak cannons with full (un-upgraded) cards, along with a +1 shred module, and happen upon an ion weapon with two starting upgraded javelins, I'm probably better off breaking the flak synergies, and utilizing a resource I only have 2 prod in. There is no (reasonable) way to upgrade my existing setup to match the output of completely switching gears or taking a weapon class that doesn't really fit the ship. It's not a bad game at all, and I hope to change this review one day, but most runs are frustrating, not fun. I don't mind losing a run whatsoever, but it feels like 90% of the outcome is RNG, and no matter how I replayed it, it wouldn't have worked.
游戏是好游戏，就是经常卡死，
奔着FTL的高清3D代餐尝试的这款游戏，但实际体验不达预期。这款游戏的完成度太低了，可以说只有画面和大体完法。任务系统，养成系统都很简陋。还有优化差，和BUG问题也常见。短期内不推荐。 幸而制作组的更新很勤快，所以游戏烂尾的概率很低。现在买下也是未来可期。

物有所值的太空背景类杀戮尖塔卡牌肉鸽游戏，我的评分是7/10，还有很多可以完善或者优化的空间，但游玩体验其实还行。 优点： 1.把卡牌分割成不同舰艇组件的设计不错，每个组件可以各司其职，加buff的负责给buff，资源拓展的就拓展资源，揍人的就揍人。可以搭配出很多抽象且神奇的bd。 2.星图路径和燃料的设计不错，合理分配燃料可以在boss战前用更多的战斗或事件来进一步成长（甚至可以走回头路，这一点必须好评） 3.战斗动画做的还不错，导弹和动能武器的打击感很强，很喜欢打一套combo出来好几个导弹砸对面身上满血秒杀的感觉。 缺点 1.别的玩家不知道，也许是个人电脑问题？但我这里从战斗对局切到地图界面，以及点击事件之后会有相当明显的卡顿，且偶尔会出现卡牌放大卡在界面中间无法选中的bug。不算严重，但确实一定程度影响游戏体验。 2.事件太少战斗太多，本来这样的搭配也没问题，但大部分事件给我一种凑数的感觉，不论是从文本还是局内资源回报来说。个人认为在高频次战斗之外的事件应该做的更精美一点，起码要起到调解游戏节奏的作用。 3.身为肉鸽游戏居然没有选择刷新选项？虽然杀戮尖塔里也没有刷新的机制... 4.外交关系的设定不错，但为什么大都是减外交关系的事件？为啥初始外交取决于开什么船啊，俺们不都是一个空间站出来的吗？如果设定全都是中立关系用事件来自由发展会更合理，但可惜并不是这样，以至于外交系统在后续游玩过程中变得毫无存在感，完全吃不到盟友红利。身为玩家就不能当所有人的好朋友吗（bushi） 5.空间站的存在有点鸡肋，空间站其实应该是流程里很重要的节点，但目前来说对游戏体验的帮助相当小，虽然功能确实也很多...怎么说呢，感觉可优化空间还很大。 总结：优缺点还挺明显的感觉，能在游戏里看到很多杀戮尖塔的影子，但说换皮的还是有点过分，制作组还是有不少小巧思的，喜欢卡牌肉鸽的可以入。 另外希望能加一点局外建设的内容，比如给我船升级一下？给初始系统加点buff？外交关系倾斜一点？诸如此类的。

Game is fun but the entirety of the map is trial and error. Half of the time the game gives no indication of when decisions matter. Sometimes it will prompt you of the results of the decision, the other times it just closes the text/dialog box and goes back to the map. And since you can only move freely on like 1/10 of the map you end up spending precious and limited fuel on something that could have been easily avoided. Also, when it does this and pushes you back out to the world map it doesn't mark off the location as a place that you will no longer have an activity, tricking you into thinking that you can try again for a different result. You can try again but the result won't change. It's one of those "illusion of choice" that I hate when games do that only drains you of resources (it will cost fuel to access it again). It's a knowledge gap trap because the game never does anything to indicate that it's basically an irreversible trap. Speaking of knowledge gap traps. There is no benefit to travelling to icons other than fights (besides docking stations and reactor upgrades). Fight icons ALWAYS reward the player for winning, while literally every other icon (outside of docking stations and reactor upgrades) are gambling to get the same the rewards you would have just got for going to a fight icon instead. Participating in every fight you can is how you actually build synergy and a proper deck so all other options are just not good in comparison. Even when going to a different location that isn't a fight icon but gives a dialog option that still results in a fight anyway it's still gambling. It will say something along the lines of "60% success rate upon winning". And with this game's XCOM success rates you effectively avoided a fight icon to go to a different location just to still fight, and then get nothing when you win. Worse case scenario, you lost resources to get there. A lot of card descriptions are vague enough to make many cards trial as well, because they sound to closely worded to cards that don't do the same thing -basically making it where you have to use it first to actually see what it's doing (voiding the purpose of the description). The game isn't complete either. Their are level systems that you can see in text but clearly aren't available to be used yet, and there are game breaking bugs like the game freezing on specific dialog options forcing you to start a new run. The game is fun but I definitely wouldn't recommend buying it unless on sale in a couple of years when they actually finish the game.
